event_checks.event: God calls Abram to leave his country
event_checks.reason: Genesis 12:1 records the LORD telling Abram to leave his country, kindred and father's house.

event_checks.event: God promises descendants like the stars
event_checks.reason: Genesis 15:5 has God telling Abram to number the stars and saying 'So shall thy seed be.'

event_checks.event: Abram's name is changed to Abraham
event_checks.reason: Genesis 17:5 states the name change explicitly.

event_checks.event: Isaac is born to Sarah
event_checks.reason: Genesis 21:3 names Isaac as the son Sarah bore to Abraham.

event_checks.event: Abraham is tested in the land of Moriah
event_checks.reason: Genesis 22:2 commands Abraham to offer Isaac in the land of Moriah. Genesis 22:1 calls this a test ('God did tempt Abraham').

event_checks.event: Jesus is taken up in a cloud
event_checks.reason: Acts 1:9 says he was taken up and a cloud received him out of their sight.

event_checks.event: The Spirit comes at Pentecost
event_checks.reason: Acts 2:1-4 describes the day of Pentecost and the disciples being filled with the Holy Ghost.

event_checks.event: A lame man is healed at the temple gate
event_checks.reason: Acts 3:6-8 describes the healing and his entering the temple. The 'gate' detail (the gate called Beautiful) is in Acts 3:2, not in the cited verses.

event_checks.event: Stephen is stoned
event_checks.reason: Acts 7:59 explicitly says they stoned Stephen.

event_checks.event: Saul meets the risen Jesus near Damascus
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:3-4 gives the light and the voice near Damascus. The speaker is identified as Jesus in Acts 9:5, which is just outside the cited range. This is a reasonable paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Ravens feed Elijah
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 17:6 states the ravens brought him bread and flesh morning and evening.

event_checks.event: The widow's meal and oil do not run out
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 17:16 states the barrel of meal wasted not and the cruse of oil did not fail.

event_checks.event: Fire falls on Mount Carmel
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 18:38 describes the fire of the LORD falling and consuming the sacrifice. Mount Carmel is not named in verse 38 itself, but the context (18:19-20) clearly places it there.

event_checks.event: Elijah hears a still small voice
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 19:12 mentions the still small voice. Elijah's hearing it is implied by 19:13.

event_checks.event: Elijah goes up by a whirlwind
event_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:11 states that Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

event_checks.event: Esther is made queen
event_checks.reason: Esther 2:17 states the king set the royal crown upon her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.

event_checks.event: Haman plots against the Jews
event_checks.reason: Esther 3:6 says Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the kingdom.

event_checks.event: Esther goes in to the king
event_checks.reason: Esther 5:2 shows Esther standing in the court and the king holding out the golden sceptre, which she touched. This matches her going in unbidden.

event_checks.event: Haman is hanged on his own gallows
event_checks.reason: Esther 7:10 says they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. The verse calls it the gallows he prepared, which fits 'his own gallows'.

event_checks.event: An angel appears to Gideon by the winepress
event_checks.reason: Judges 6:11-12 states that the angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon as he threshed wheat by the winepress.

event_checks.event: Gideon tests God with a fleece
event_checks.reason: Judges 6:37 records Gideon proposing the fleece test.

event_checks.event: God reduces the army to three hundred
event_checks.reason: Judges 7:7 says God will save Israel by the three hundred who lapped and send the others home. The reduction is the culmination of the process begun in 7:2-6.

event_checks.event: Trumpets sound and pitchers are broken
event_checks.reason: Judges 7:20 describes the three companies blowing trumpets and breaking pitchers.

event_checks.event: Daniel refuses the king's meat
event_checks.reason: Daniel 1:8 states Daniel purposed not to defile himself with the king's meat and wine.

event_checks.event: Daniel interprets the dream of the great image
event_checks.reason: In Daniel 2:31 Daniel is speaking to the king, recounting the dream of the great image as part of making it known. The interpretation itself follows in vv. 36-45. This is minor and acceptable.

event_checks.event: Three friends are cast into the furnace
event_checks.reason: Daniel 3:23 says Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego fell down bound into the burning fiery furnace.

event_checks.event: Fingers write on the palace wall
event_checks.reason: Daniel 5:5 describes the fingers of a man's hand writing on the plaister of the wall of the king's palace.

event_checks.event: Daniel is cast into the den of lions
event_checks.reason: Daniel 6:16 says they brought Daniel and cast him into the den of lions.

event_checks.event: Samuel anoints David
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:13 explicitly states that Samuel anointed David with the horn of oil.

event_checks.event: David plays the harp for Saul
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:23 states that David took a harp and played, and Saul was refreshed.

event_checks.event: David defeats Goliath
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:50 states that David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and stone and slew him.

event_checks.event: David spares Saul in the cave
event_checks.reason: 24:4 shows David cutting off Saul's skirt instead of killing him. The sparing is explicit in 24:6-7 and 24:10, so the event is clearly within the cited episode, but the cited verse alone only implies it.

event_checks.event: David is anointed king over Israel
event_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 5:3 states that the elders anointed David king over Israel at Hebron.

suggested_fix: Optional: cite 1 Samuel 24:4-7 or 24:10 for the cave event, so the sparing is explicit in the quoted text. Some scholars debate whether the harp episode came chronologically before the Goliath episode (because of 17:55-58). However, the text's sequence (16:21-23 followed by 17:15) supports the stated order.

event_checks.event: Light is divided from darkness
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:3-5 says God divided the light from the darkness on the first day.

event_checks.event: The firmament divides the waters
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:6-8 says the firmament divided the waters under it from the waters above it on the second day.

event_checks.event: Dry land appears and plants grow
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:9-13 says the dry land appeared and the earth brought forth grass, herbs and trees on the third day.

event_checks.event: The sun, moon and stars are set in the sky
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:14-19 describes the two great lights and the stars set in the firmament on the fourth day. 'Sun' and 'moon' are a fair paraphrase of the greater and lesser lights.

event_checks.event: Sea creatures and birds are created
event_checks.reason: Genesis 1:20-23 says the waters brought forth living creatures, including great whales, and that winged fowl were created on the fifth day.

suggested_fix: The events and their order (Days 1-5) are accurate and unambiguous. The hint 'The first event is in Genesis 1' gives the player no help, because every event is in Genesis 1. Replace it with something useful, such as 'Each event happened on a separate day, from the first day to the fifth day.' or 'Light came first, on the first day (Genesis 1:3-5).' Also tidy the reference_label from 'Genesis 1 – Genesis 1' to 'Genesis 1:3-23'. Optionally retitle to 'The First Five Days of Creation', since Days 6-7 are not included.

event_checks.event: Jacob is born holding Esau's heel
event_checks.reason: Genesis 25:26 says his hand took hold on Esau's heel and he was called Jacob.

event_checks.event: Esau sells his birthright for pottage
event_checks.reason: Genesis 25:33-34 says Esau sold his birthright and Jacob gave him bread and pottage of lentiles.

event_checks.event: Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven
event_checks.reason: Genesis 28:12 describes a ladder reaching to heaven, with angels ascending and descending on it.

event_checks.event: Jacob wrestles and is renamed Israel
event_checks.reason: Genesis 32:28 gives the renaming. The wrestling itself is in 32:24-25, which is not quoted, though it is the immediate context. This is acceptable as paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Baby Moses is placed among the bulrushes
event_checks.reason: Exodus 2:3 says his mother put him in an ark of bulrushes and laid it in the flags by the river's brink. 'Among the bulrushes' is an acceptable paraphrase.

event_checks.event: God speaks from the burning bush
event_checks.reason: Exodus 3:2 describes the angel of the LORD appearing in the burning bush but records no speech. God calls to Moses out of the bush in Exodus 3:4, which would be a more precise citation.

event_checks.event: The river is turned to blood
event_checks.reason: Exodus 7:20 explicitly states that all the waters in the river were turned to blood.

event_checks.event: The first Passover is kept
event_checks.reason: Exodus 12:13 is God's instruction and promise about the blood, not the actual keeping. Israel's obedience is recorded in Exodus 12:28 and 12:50, and Exodus 12:27 explicitly names the Passover sacrifice. The event is clearly Passover-related, so it is supported in substance.

event_checks.event: Israel crosses the Red Sea on dry ground
event_checks.reason: Exodus 14:22 states Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground.

event_checks.event: God calls Jonah to go to Nineveh
event_checks.reason: Jonah 1:2 records the LORD commanding Jonah to arise and go to Nineveh.

event_checks.event: Jonah flees toward Tarshish
event_checks.reason: Jonah 1:3 states Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish and boarded a ship at Joppa.

event_checks.event: A great fish swallows Jonah
event_checks.reason: Jonah 1:17 says the LORD prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah.

event_checks.event: Jonah warns Nineveh: forty days
event_checks.reason: Jonah 3:4 records Jonah crying, 'Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.'

event_checks.event: God prepares a gourd to shade Jonah
event_checks.reason: Jonah 4:6 says the LORD God prepared a gourd to be a shadow over his head.

event_checks.event: Rahab hides the spies in Jericho
event_checks.reason: Joshua 2:1-4 states that Joshua sent two spies to Jericho, that they lodged in Rahab's house, and that 'the woman took the two men, and hid them.'

event_checks.event: Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground
event_checks.reason: Joshua 3:17 states that 'all the Israelites passed over on dry ground.'

event_checks.event: The walls of Jericho fall
event_checks.reason: Joshua 6:20 states that 'the wall fell down flat' and the people took the city.

event_checks.event: The sun stands still at Gibeon
event_checks.reason: Joshua 10:13 describes the sun standing still but does not name Gibeon. Gibeon is named in 10:12 ('Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon'). The event is accurate, but the cited verse alone does not fully support the wording.

event_checks.event: Jesus is baptized
event_checks.reason: Matthew 3:16 explicitly describes Jesus being baptized and coming up out of the water.

event_checks.event: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness
event_checks.reason: Matthew 4:1 states Jesus was led into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.

event_checks.event: Jesus calls fishermen to be fishers of men
event_checks.reason: Matthew 4:19 contains 'I will make you fishers of men,' spoken to Peter and Andrew, who were fishermen (4:18).

event_checks.event: Jesus teaches on the mountain
event_checks.reason: Matthew 5:1 has Jesus going up into a mountain. Verse 2 states he taught them. Minor extrapolation from the cited verse, but the passage clearly supports it.

event_checks.event: God tells Noah to build an ark of gopher wood
event_checks.reason: Genesis 6:14 directly commands Noah to make an ark of gopher wood.

event_checks.event: Noah's family and the animals go into the ark
event_checks.reason: Genesis 7:7-9 describes Noah, his wife, his sons and their wives, and the animals going in two and two.

event_checks.event: Rain falls for forty days and forty nights
event_checks.reason: Genesis 7:12 states the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.

event_checks.event: A dove returns with an olive leaf
event_checks.reason: Genesis 8:11 describes the dove returning in the evening with an olive leaf in her mouth.

event_checks.event: God sets His bow in the cloud as a covenant sign
event_checks.reason: Genesis 9:13 says 'I do set my bow in the cloud... for a token of a covenant.'

event_checks.event: Crowds cry Hosanna as Jesus enters Jerusalem
event_checks.reason: Matthew 21:9 records the multitudes crying Hosanna, in the context of the triumphal entry (21:10 confirms he came into Jerusalem).

event_checks.event: Jesus breaks bread at the Last Supper
event_checks.reason: Matthew 26:26 records Jesus taking bread, blessing, breaking and giving it during the meal.

event_checks.event: Jesus prays in Gethsemane
event_checks.reason: Matthew 26:36 has Jesus come to Gethsemane and go to pray. The prayer itself is in 26:39, but the cited verse supports the event.

event_checks.event: Jesus is crucified
event_checks.reason: Matthew 27:35 states 'they crucified him.'

event_checks.event: The angel says: He is not here, for he is risen
event_checks.reason: Matthew 28:6 contains these words. The speaker is the angel of 28:2-5, whose speech begins in 28:5.

event_checks.event: Jacob gives Joseph a coat of many colours
event_checks.reason: Genesis 37:3 says Israel (Jacob) 'made him a coat of many colours.'

event_checks.event: Joseph's brothers sell him for twenty pieces of silver
event_checks.reason: The cited verse confirms the sale for twenty pieces of silver, but its grammar is ambiguous: it could be read as the Midianites drawing Joseph out and selling him. The brothers' role is supported by context (37:27, 'Come, and let us sell him') and by 45:4 ('whom ye sold into Egypt'). This is acceptable for the quiz.

event_checks.event: Joseph serves in Potiphar's house
event_checks.reason: Genesis 39:1 records Potiphar buying Joseph. His service in Potiphar's house is stated in 39:2-4 ('he was in the house of his master'). This is a reasonable paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dream
event_checks.reason: Genesis 41:25 begins Joseph's interpretation of Pharaoh's dream.

event_checks.event: Joseph reveals himself to his brothers
event_checks.reason: Genesis 45:4: 'I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.'

event_checks.event: Waters turned to blood
event_checks.reason: Exodus 7:20 explicitly states the waters in the river were turned to blood.

event_checks.event: Frogs cover the land
event_checks.reason: Exodus 8:6 says the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.

event_checks.event: Dust becomes lice
event_checks.reason: Exodus 8:17 says the dust of the earth became lice throughout all the land.

event_checks.event: Thick darkness for three days
event_checks.reason: Exodus 10:22 says there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days.

event_checks.event: Death of the firstborn
event_checks.reason: Exodus 12:29 says the LORD smote all the firstborn at midnight.

event_checks.event: Gabriel announces Jesus' birth to Mary
event_checks.reason: Luke 1:31 gives the announcement of the conception and birth of a son named JESUS. Gabriel is named as the speaker in the surrounding context (Luke 1:26-27), though not in this verse itself.

event_checks.event: Joseph and Mary travel to Bethlehem
event_checks.reason: Luke 2:4 states Joseph went up from Nazareth to Bethlehem. Mary's accompanying him is in the adjoining verse 2:5, which is a reasonable paraphrase.

event_checks.event: Angels appear to shepherds
event_checks.reason: Luke 2:8-9 describes 'the angel of the Lord' (singular) appearing to the shepherds. The plural 'angels' is only supported by the multitude of the heavenly host in 2:13. This is a minor paraphrase and acceptable.

event_checks.event: Simeon holds the child in the temple
event_checks.reason: Luke 2:25-28 states Simeon took the child up in his arms in the temple.

event_checks.event: The twelve-year-old Jesus is found in the temple
event_checks.reason: Luke 2:42-46 directly describes this event.

event_checks.event: Saul is converted near Damascus
event_checks.reason: Acts 9:3 shows Saul journeying near Damascus when a light from heaven shines round about him, the start of his conversion account. The surrounding verses complete the conversion, so 'converted' is a fair summary.

event_checks.event: Barnabas and Saul are separated for the work
event_checks.reason: Acts 13:2 directly records the Holy Ghost saying 'Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work.'

event_checks.event: Paul sees a vision of a man of Macedonia
event_checks.reason: Acts 16:9 explicitly describes the night vision of a man of Macedonia.

event_checks.event: Paul preaches on Mars' hill in Athens
event_checks.reason: Acts 17:22 has Paul standing in the midst of Mars' hill addressing the men of Athens.

event_checks.event: Paul is shipwrecked on Melita
event_checks.reason: Acts 28:1 records their escape and naming the island Melita. The shipwreck itself is narrated in Acts 27:41-44, so the cited verse implies rather than states the shipwreck. This is acceptable paraphrase.

event_checks.event: A traveller falls among thieves
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:30 says a certain man going from Jerusalem to Jericho fell among thieves. Calling him a 'traveller' is a fair paraphrase.

event_checks.event: A priest passes by
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:31 says a priest came down that way and passed by on the other side.

event_checks.event: A Levite passes by
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:32 says a Levite came, looked on him, and passed by on the other side.

event_checks.event: A Samaritan binds up his wounds
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:33-34 says the Samaritan bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine.

event_checks.event: He pays the host two pence
event_checks.reason: Luke 10:35 says on the morrow he took out two pence and gave them to the host.

event_checks.event: An angel announces a Nazarite son
event_checks.reason: Judges 13:5 records the announcement of a son who would be a Nazarite from the womb. Judges 13:3 identifies the speaker as the angel of the LORD.

event_checks.event: Samson tears a young lion
event_checks.reason: Judges 14:5-6 says he rent the young lion as he would have rent a kid.

event_checks.event: Samson loves Delilah
event_checks.reason: Judges 16:4 says he loved a woman named Delilah.

event_checks.event: Samson brings down the house
event_checks.reason: Judges 16:30 says the house fell upon the lords and the people.

event_checks.event: The younger son asks for his portion
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:12 states the younger son asked, 'Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me.'

event_checks.event: He wastes his substance with riotous living
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:13 says he 'wasted his substance with riotous living' in a far country.

event_checks.event: He feeds swine in a far country
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:15 says he joined a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed swine. Verse 13 establishes the far country.

event_checks.event: His father runs to embrace him
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:20 says the father 'ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him', which fairly supports 'embrace'.

event_checks.event: The elder brother is angry
event_checks.reason: Luke 15:28 says 'he was angry, and would not go in'. The context (vv. 25-28) confirms this is the elder son.

suggested_fix: The events, references and order are all correct and unambiguous. The hint 'The first event is in Luke 15.' gives no help, because every event is in Luke 15. Replace it with something useful, such as 'The story begins with a request for an inheritance (Luke 15:12).' Also simplify the redundant reference_label 'Luke 15 – Luke 15' to 'Luke 15:11-32'.

event_checks.event: Hannah prays and makes a vow
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:10-11 records Hannah praying in bitterness of soul and vowing to give a son to the LORD.

event_checks.event: The LORD calls the boy Samuel
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 3:10 records the LORD calling 'Samuel, Samuel' and Samuel answering.

event_checks.event: Samuel anoints Saul
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 10:1 records Samuel pouring oil on 'his head'. The verse itself does not name Saul, but the context (1 Samuel 9-10) makes clear it is Saul, so this is acceptable.

event_checks.event: Samuel anoints David
event_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:13 explicitly records Samuel anointing David with the horn of oil.

event_checks.event: Ruth vows to go with Naomi
event_checks.reason: Ruth 1:16 records Ruth's vow: 'whither thou goest, I will go... thy people shall be my people.'

event_checks.event: Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz
event_checks.reason: Ruth 2:3 says she gleaned and 'her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz.'

event_checks.event: Ruth asks Boaz to spread his skirt over her
event_checks.reason: Ruth 3:9 has Ruth say 'spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.'

event_checks.event: Boaz marries Ruth
event_checks.reason: Ruth 4:13 says 'Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife.'

event_checks.event: Obed is born
event_checks.reason: Ruth 4:17 names the son born as Obed. The birth itself is first mentioned in 4:13, but it clearly follows the marriage, so the order is unaffected.

event_checks.event: The women find the stone rolled away
event_checks.reason: Luke 24:2-3 says they found the stone rolled away and did not find the body.

event_checks.event: Two disciples walk to Emmaus
event_checks.reason: Luke 24:13 says two of them went that same day to Emmaus.

event_checks.event: Jesus stands among the disciples: Peace be unto you
event_checks.reason: Luke 24:36 says Jesus stood in the midst of them and said, Peace be unto you.

event_checks.event: Jesus is carried up into heaven
event_checks.reason: Luke 24:51 says he was parted from them and carried up into heaven.

event_checks.event: Solomon asks for an understanding heart
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 3:9 records Solomon's request for an understanding heart at Gibeon.

event_checks.event: Solomon judges between two mothers
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 3:25 is part of the account of the two harlots (3:16-28), which follows the Gibeon dream.

event_checks.event: Solomon builds the house of the LORD
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 6:14 states Solomon built and finished the house. This is the temple construction of chapter 6.

event_checks.event: The temple is dedicated
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 8:63 explicitly says the king and Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.

event_checks.event: The queen of Sheba visits
event_checks.reason: 1 Kings 10:1 records the queen of Sheba coming to prove Solomon.

event_checks.event: God provides manna
event_checks.reason: Exodus 16:15 explicitly names the manna as the bread the LORD has given Israel to eat.

event_checks.event: The Ten Commandments are given at Sinai
event_checks.reason: Exodus 20:3 is the first commandment, so it belongs to the giving of the Ten Commandments. The verse itself does not mention Sinai, but the surrounding context (Exodus 19–20) does. This is acceptable.

event_checks.event: The people make a golden calf
event_checks.reason: Exodus 32:4 records the molten calf being fashioned and the people proclaiming it as their gods. Aaron did the actual fashioning, but the people supplied the gold and are credited with it (cf. Exodus 32:35, 'they made the calf, which Aaron made'), so the paraphrase is fair.

event_checks.event: Twelve spies are sent to search Canaan
event_checks.reason: Numbers 13:2 commands sending one man from every tribe to search Canaan, which means twelve men. The sending itself follows in 13:3, 17.
